summary: Create topic-driven Slack namespace with Jira-triggered Confluence seed + thread-pruner automation
description:
Request: Set up a curated, topic-driven Slack namespace and automation that: 1) provisions a Slack channel + Confluence seed page + Jira epic when a team requests a new 'topic' via a lightweight intake form, 2) applies per-channel retention/visibility policies based on topic tags, and 3) runs a thread-pruner bot that trims unresolved threads older than 90 days into an archival Confluence page (for audit) and posts a summary to the channel once pruning completes.

Impact: This will reduce noise from long-lived, ad-hoc channels, centralize onboarding artifacts for each topic, and ensure auditability for compliance reviews. Intended customers are internal teams that spin up short-lived research or project channels (research pods, eval experiments, cross-pod task forces).

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- A new Slack namespace (topic-*) is provisionable via the existing onboarding form.
- On intake approval a channel is created, Confluence seed populated from a templated page, and a Jira epic created and linked.
- Channel gets metadata tags (topic:, retention:) visible to admins.
- Thread-pruner bot runs weekly and archives threads >90 days to a Confluence archival page and posts a one-line summary back to the channel.
- Owners can opt-in/out per channel and request extended retention via a lightweight approval flow.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - provisioning request. Walkthrough considered: 1) Submit intake form prototype at /forms/topic-channel 2) Observe automated channel + artifacts creation 3) Inspect metadata tags and retention settings 4) Simulate thread age >90d in staging to test pruner behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Per-channel retention tag set according to template
Thread-pruner archives threads >90 days to Confluence and posts summary
investigation_notes:
Initial feasibility review: Slack API supports channel creation + custom channel topics; retention enforcement requires admin integration with corporate retention tool or Slack EKM—we can implement soft-retention via a bot that copies content to Confluence and then pins a summary, but permanent deletions will need Legal/Security sign-off.

Prototype work: Lina created a proof-of-concept repo (see PR #418) that provisions channels and a seeded Confluence page. Concourse job can be triggered from intake form.

Open questions:
- Does Security require that archival pages for pruned threads be stored in a restricted Confluence space?
- Are there each-team retention exceptions we need to encode in the intake form?
